name: Agarita

facts.when: Flowers February to March, fruit April to May
facts.where: Dry brushland, rocky slopes, Hill Country and west

caution: Stiff spines on every leaf tip. Wear gloves, or better, use the sheet trick.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Nobody picks agarita berries one at a time. Spread a sheet under the bush, tap the branches with a stick, and let the ripe fruit fall. Winnow out the leaves and you can gather a jelly batch in twenty minutes.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The berries are tart and bright, closer to a currant than a blueberry. Classic uses are jelly and syrup; the strained juice also ferments into a pale country wine.

sections.title: Identification notes
sections.body: Three-part leaves, each leaflet tipped with holly-like spines, blue-green reading gray at a distance. With red berries present there is no dangerous look-alike in Texas.
